analysis.description: The paper proposes an active learning algorithm leveraging GFlowNets and epistemic uncertainty estimation to generate diverse batches of biological sequences, incorporating existing labeled datasets to accelerate learning. It demonstrates the approach on several biological sequence design tasks, finding it generates more diverse and novel high-scoring candidates compared to existing methods.

type.justification: The paper conducts empirical studies and presents empirical results on various biological sequence design tasks, validating the effectiveness of the GFlowNet-AL algorithm.
type.quote: We present empirical results on several biological sequence design tasks, and we find that our method generates more diverse and novel batches with high scoring candidates compared to existing approaches.
